newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels deny making peace moves.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels deny making peace moves.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels on Tuesday denied sending a group of emissaries to Sri Lanka with a letter consenting to peace talks after government troops launched an new offensive in the north.

Newspaper reports said that the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, had sent a delegation to initiate peace talks with President Chandrika Kumaratunga and opposition United National Party leader Ranil Wickeremesinghe.

"We deny that we have made any efforts to send any emissaries to Colombo to have discussions with the government or the opposition or anybody," the LTTE's international spokesman Anton Rajah told Reuters from London by telephone.
The Sunday Times said the letter was signed by Anton Balasingham, LTTE's advisor based in northern Sri Lanka and their political wing chief Thamil Chelvam.
But Rajah said there ware no moves for peace talks with the government.
"The LTTE denies that Balasingham has sent a letter asking to meet the opposition leader or the government for any talks," he said.

Sri Lankan troops launched a major offensive last week to open a land supply route between northern Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, and Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
Peace talks between Kumaratunga's People's Alliance government and the LTTE broke down in April 1995 after the rebels sank two navy boats in the eastern Trincomalee harbour.
The government says that more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the number is higher.
